body.purpose: Readable descriptions, navigation, metadata, and controls.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The confident immediate action, such as Play or View.
components.html: <button class="ds-button ds-button-primary" type="button"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="m6 3 14 9-14 9V3Z"/></svg>Play now</button>

components.name: Accent Button
components.description: Committed flow progression, such as Create, Continue, or Submit.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Outlined secondary work that remains clearly interactive on the midnight canvas.
components.html: <button class="ds-button ds-button-secondary" type="button"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg>Save to library</button>

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: A low-emphasis text destination with a quiet tonal response.
components.html: <button class="ds-button ds-button-ghost" type="button">View details <svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M5 12h14m-6-6 6 6-6 6"/></svg></button>

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: A muted destructive action that communicates consequence without alarmist saturation.
components.html: <button class="ds-button ds-button-danger" type="button"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M3 6h18M8 6V4h8v2m-9 0 1 14h8l1-14M10 10v6m4-6v6"/></svg>Delete list</button>

components.name: Global Navigation
components.description: An 84px flat desktop shell that becomes a separate 64px brand-and-menu bar below 1024px; search and profile move inside the right-side dialog.

components.name: Label and Input
components.description: A persistent tracked label paired with a quiet 52px native field across empty, filled, invalid, read-only, and disabled states.
components.html: <label class="ds-label" for="display-name">Display name</label><input class="ds-input" id="display-name" name="displayName" type="text" autocomplete="name" placeholder="What should people call you?" />
components.css: .ds-label{display:block;color:var(--consumit-copy,#c9c4bc);font:700 12px/20px 'DejaVu Sans',Arial,sans-serif;letter-spacing:.12em;text-transform:uppercase}.ds-input{box-sizing:border-box;display:block;width:100%;min-width:0;height:52px;margin-top:8px;padding:0 16px;border:1px solid var(--consumit-control-outline,rgba(244,240,232,.4));border-radius:var(--consumit-radius-control,6px);outline:0;background:var(--consumit-field,#0d0d10);color:var(--consumit-ink,#f4f0e8);font:400 14px/1 'DejaVu Sans',Arial,sans-serif;transition:background-color 150ms ease-out,border-color 150ms ease-out,box-shadow 150ms ease-out}.ds-input::placeholder{color:var(--consumit-muted,#85817c)}.ds-input:hover{border-color:rgba(244,240,232,.6)}.ds-input:focus-visible{border-color:var(--consumit-orange,#ff5d38);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--consumit-canvas,#09090b),0 0 0 3px rgba(255,93,56,.3)}.ds-input[aria-invalid=true]{border-color:var(--consumit-danger,#8e5450)}.ds-input[aria-invalid=true]:focus-visible{border-color:var(--consumit-danger,#8e5450);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--consumit-canvas,#09090b),0 0 0 3px rgba(142,84,80,.4)}.ds-input:read-only{background:var(--consumit-surface,#121216)}.ds-input:disabled{cursor:not-allowed;border-color:var(--consumit-border,rgba(255,255,255,.1));background:var(--consumit-surface,#121216);color:var(--consumit-muted,#85817c);opacity:.6}.ds-input:-webkit-autofill{box-shadow:0 0 0 1000px var(--consumit-field,#0d0d10) inset;-webkit-text-fill-color:var(--consumit-ink,#f4f0e8);caret-color:var(--consumit-orange,#ff5d38)}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-input{transition:none}}

narrative.overview:
Consumit feels cinematic, editorial, and human: a near-black room lit by warm ivory type and rare signals of color. The interface is intimate rather than glossy, with enough quiet space for artwork, taste, and other people’s perspectives to carry emotional weight.

The system pairs decisive controls with restrained surfaces. It should feel alive with other people’s taste without becoming noisy, gamified, or generically “streaming app.” Generic dashboards and glossy-tech decoration are explicit anti-references.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black, flat surfaces with warm editorial contrast
Charter display type paired with compact DejaVu Sans controls
Rare orange action signals with semantically reserved lilac and lime
Purposeful composition that becomes distinct on mobile

rules.name: The Scarce Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange communicates brand, selection, progress, or commitment; it is never ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Semantic Accent Rule
rules.body: Lilac means social or taste context, and lime means presence, health, or success. Do not swap their jobs for variety.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif type tells the story; sans-serif type helps the member act.

rules.name: The Flat Interface Rule
rules.body: Shadows may separate artwork, but ordinary controls and content panels remain flat.

rules.name: The Perceptible Control Rule
rules.body: Interactive boundaries use the dedicated control outline and keep a minimum 44px target; faint separators only divide passive content.

rules.name: The Human Signal Rule
rules.body: Presence, save state, status, rank, and compatibility are expressed in text as well as color or iconography.

rules.name: The Artwork Leads Rule
rules.body: Supplied artwork preserves its intended aspect ratio and leads media compositions; gradients exist only to protect artwork legibility.

rules.name: The Social Context Rule
rules.body: Taste and social components explain why content matters through named people and readable context rather than anonymous engagement totals.

dos: Do use the supplied brand and artwork assets instead of recreating them with generic icons.
Do reserve ivory for confident immediate actions and orange for committed progression.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, touch-safe control heights, and readable metadata contrast.
Do finish each shared component and its states before composing the next screen.
donts: Don't introduce large pills, routine gradients, glass effects, or floating dashboard cards.
Don't use orange, lilac, or lime as interchangeable decoration.
Don't reduce every surface to a rounded card grid.
Don't treat mobile as a scaled-down desktop composition.
